subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Metastatic hormone receptor-positive breast cancer: endocrine combinations, ESR1 and PIK3CA alterations and antibody-drug conjugates

steps.tx: First-line systemic therapy for metastatic hormone receptor-positive breast cancer provides combined treatment with an aromatase inhibitor and CDK4/6 inhibitors **palbociclib**, **ribociclib**, or **abemaciclib**. Landmark randomized phase III trials PALOMA-2, MONALEESA-2, and MONARCH-3 demonstrated that CDK4/6 inhibition dramatically prolongs median progression-free survival beyond 2 years, establishing endocrine combination regimens as the undisputed first-line standard.
steps.say: First-line systemic therapy for metastatic hormone receptor-positive breast cancer provides combined treatment with an aromatase inhibitor and CDK4/6 inhibitors palbociclib, ribociclib, or abemaciclib. Landmark randomized phase III trials PALOMA-2, MONALEESA-2, and MONARCH-3 demonstrated that CDK4/6 inhibition dramatically prolongs median progression-free survival beyond 2 years, establishing endocrine combination regimens as the undisputed first-line standard.

steps.tx: Among CDK4/6 inhibitors, **Ribociclib** combined with endocrine therapy is the first agent to establish a statistically significant **overall survival** benefit in advanced HR-positive breast cancer. In MONALEESA-2, ribociclib plus letrozole prolonged median overall survival to 63.9 months compared to 51.4 months with placebo, demonstrating an absolute 12.5-month overall survival prolongation that persisted across premenopausal cohorts in MONALEESA-7.

right.title: Endocrine Monotherapy
points: Higher rate of early endocrine failure

steps.tx: Intramuscular **Fulvestrant** combined with abemaciclib, ribociclib, or palbociclib represents the established **standard of care** for second-line metastatic HR+ breast cancer progressing on aromatase inhibitors. In randomized phase III trials PALOMA-3, MONALEESA-3, and MONARCH-2, combining fulvestrant with CDK4/6 inhibitors significantly prolonged progression-free survival and overall survival compared to endocrine monotherapy.

steps.tx: Acquired point mutations in the **ESR1** ligand-binding domain, such as Y537S and D538G, constitutively activate estrogen receptor transcription independently of circulating estrogens, conferring resistance to aromatase inhibitors. In the phase III **EMERALD** trial, the oral selective estrogen receptor degrader **elacestrant** significantly improved progression-free survival over standard endocrine therapy in patients harbouring detectable ESR1 mutations.

left.title: ESR1 Mutant Biology
points: Emerges under selective pressure of aromatase inhibitors

right.title: Elacestrant Oral SERD
points: Binds mutant ER; promotes receptor degradation
First oral SERD approved for ESR1-mutated cancer
Superior PFS in EMERALD vs fulvestrant or AI
Oral daily administration without depot injections

steps.tx: Mutant **oestrogen receptors** stay switched on without hormone because changes at key positions lock the binding pocket open. **Elacestrant tablets** fit that pocket and force a shape change that invites **ubiquitin labels**, sending the receptor to the **cell recycling unit** for shredding. With the receptor gone, DNA response elements stay silent and growth transcription stops, restoring control after aromatase drugs have failed.
steps.say: Certain receptor mutations keep the oestrogen receptor active without any hormone present, so aromatase drugs lose effect. Elacestrant binds the mutant pocket and twists the receptor into a shape the cell marks for disposal. The tagged receptor is destroyed in the proteasome and can no longer switch on DNA transcription. This degradation strategy improves control in mutation bearing cancers after prior hormone therapy.

vis.alt: A molecular sequence shows oral drug binding the mutant receptor, tagging it for destruction and silencing DNA transcription.
vis.caption: Sequence shows mutant receptor binding, disposal and silenced growth signaling. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Activating mutations in the alpha-catalytic subunit of PI3K encoded by **PIK3CA** occur in approximately 40% of HR-positive advanced breast cancers. In the phase III **SOLAR-1 trial**, adding the alpha-specific PI3K inhibitor **alpelisib** to fulvestrant doubled progression-free survival in PIK3CA-mutated disease from 5.7 months to 11.0 months. Key treatment-emergent adverse events include severe hyperglycaemia, maculopapular rash requiring prophylactic antihistamines, and gastrointestinal diarrhoea.

steps.tx: Targeting the downstream AKT node, the phase III **CAPItello-291** trial evaluated the potent pan-AKT kinase inhibitor **capivasertib** combined with fulvestrant. In patients harboring one or more alterations in **PIK3CA**, AKT1, or PTEN, capivasertib plus fulvestrant significantly prolonged progression-free survival from 3.1 to 7.3 months, establishing an effective targeted option for patients progressing through CDK4/6 inhibitors.

steps.tx: The landmark phase III **DESTINY-Breast04** trial fundamentally redefined therapy by establishing the antibody-drug conjugate **Trastuzumab deruxtecan** in **HER2-low** metastatic breast cancer. Defined by immunohistochemistry as IHC 1+ or IHC 2+ with negative FISH, HER2-low tumours treated with trastuzumab deruxtecan demonstrated dramatic, unprecedented improvements in both progression-free survival and overall survival compared to physician-choice chemotherapy.

points: Topoisomerase I inhibitor exatecan derivative payload
High drug-to-antibody ratio of 8:1 with cleavable linker
Bystander antitumor killing effect on adjacent cells

right.title: Clinical Efficacy (DESTINY-Breast04)

steps.tx: Oral mTORC1 inhibitor **Everolimus** inhibits the downstream serine/threonine kinase mammalian target of rapamycin. In the phase III **BOLERO-2** trial, adding everolimus to the steroidal aromatase inhibitor exemestane more than doubled progression-free survival in patients with endocrine-refractory metastatic breast cancer. Class-specific adverse effects include aphthous stomatitis, non-infectious pneumonitis, hyperglycaemia, and hyperlipidaemia requiring active supportive management.
